The '''2019–20 Primeira Liga''' (also known as '''Liga NOS''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 86th season of the [[Primeira Liga]], the top professional league for Portuguese [[association football]] clubs. The season started on 9 August 2019 and was finished on 26 July 2020.

[[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] were the defending champions, after winning their 37th league title in the [[2018–19 Primeira Liga|previous season]]. [[F.C. Paços de Ferreira|Paços de Ferreira]] and [[F.C. Famalicão|Famalicão]] were promoted from the second-tier [[2018–19 LigaPro]], while [[Gil Vicente F.C.|Gil Vicente]] were promoted directly from the third-tier [[2018–19 Campeonato de Portugal]] by court decision. They replaced [[G.D. Chaves|Chaves]], [[C.D. Nacional|Nacional]] and [[C.D. Feirense|Feirense]], who were relegated to the [[2019–20 LigaPro]].

On 12 March 2020, the [[Liga Portuguesa de Futebol Profissional]] (LPFP) suspended the Primeira Liga due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]. Following the government's approval, the league resumed play on 3 June, with matches of the remaining ten matchdays taking place [[Behind closed doors (sport)|behind closed doors]].<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://desporto.sapo.pt/futebol/primeira-liga/artigos/ja-ha-programa-para-regresso-do-futebol-fc-porto-joga-no-dia-03-benfica-e-sporting-e-sporting-no-dia-seguinte|title=Oficial: Já há programa para regresso do futebol. FC Porto joga dia 3, Benfica e Sporting no dia seguinte|website=SAPO Desporto}}</ref>

On 15 July 2020, [[FC Porto|Porto]] secured their 29th league title with two matches remaining after defeating [[Sporting CP]] 2–0 at home.

After the end of the season, on 26 July, [[C.D. Aves|Desportivo das Aves]] and [[Portimonense S.C.|Portimonense]] were relegated to the [[2020–21 LigaPro]]. However, two days later, Desportivo das Aves and [[Vitória F.C.|Vitória de Setubal]] were relegated to the [[2020–21 Campeonato de Portugal]] by decision of the [[Liga Portuguesa de Futebol Profissional]] ("LPFP") after both clubs failed to meet the necessary requirements to obtain a licence for registration to participate in professional domestic competitions.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cmjornal.pt/desporto/futebol/amp/vitoria-de-setubal-e-aves-despromovidos-ao-campeonato-de-portugal|title=Vitória de Setúbal e Aves despromovidos ao Campeonato de Portugal - Futebol|access-date=29 July 2020|archive-date=11 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200911151347/https://www.cmjornal.pt/desporto/futebol/amp/vitoria-de-setubal-e-aves-despromovidos-ao-campeonato-de-portugal|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Effects of the COVID-19 pandemic==
Due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]], on 10 March 2020, the LPFP announced that all fixtures on matchday 24 (6–8 March) would be played [[Behind closed doors (sport)|behind closed doors]] following the [[Portuguese government]] to suspend events in open spaces with more than 5,000 people, as well as events behind closed doors with more than 1,000 participants, until 3 April.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dn.pt/desportos/jogos-de-futebol-a-porta-fechada-em-portugal-na-proxima-jornada-11908070.html|title=Jogos de futebol à porta fechada em Portugal na próxima jornada - DN|website=www.dn.pt|date=10 March 2020 }}</ref> Two days later, the LPFP suspended the Primeira Liga and [[LigaPro]] until further notice because of effects of the coronavirus pandemic in Portugal. The decision was taken following the [[Portuguese Football Federation]] ("FPF")'s announcement of suspending their own non-professional football and futsal competitions and also due to an emergency meeting between the Sindicato dos Jogadores Profissionais de Futebol ("SJPF"), the LPFP and the FPF to monitor the situation, in view of the proposal to suspend all sports competitions, which the SJPF added that in case of infection, there would be an aggravated loss.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://desporto.sapo.pt/futebol/primeira-liga/artigos/i-e-ii-liga-suspensa|title=Covid-19: I e II Liga suspensas por tempo indeterminado|website=SAPO Desporto}}</ref> Shortly after, LPFP president [[Pedro Proença]] met with several presidents of Primeira Liga's clubs to assess the impact of the stoppage of professional championships due to the COVID-19 pandemic. He revealed a COVID-19 economic support plan to support the treasury of various clubs in the Primeira Liga and LigaPro.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rtp.pt/noticias/futebol-nacional/covid-19-proenca-e-presidentes-de-sad-avaliam-efeitos-da-paragem_d1212688|title=Covid-19. Proença e presidentes de SAD avaliam efeitos da paragem|first=Rádio e Televisão de|last=Portugal|website=Covid-19. Proença e presidentes de SAD avaliam efeitos da paragem|date=17 March 2020 }}</ref> Afterwards, the LPFP announced the creation of an Economic Impact Monitoring Group that would be responsible for presenting measures to support the clubs that competed in the Primeira Liga and LigaPro.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sicnoticias.pt/especiais/coronavirus/2020-03-16-Covid-19-prejuizos-de-milhoes-no-futebol|title=SIC Notícias &#124; Covid-19: prejuízos de milhões no futebol|website=SIC Notícias|date=16 March 2020 }}</ref> The FPF also opened a credit line to support the finances of non-professional football and futsal clubs in the amount of one million euros to minimize the effects of the pandemic on their finances.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sicnoticias.pt/especiais/coronavirus/2020-03-16-Federacao-Portuguesa-de-Futebol-abre-linha-de-credito-para-apoiar-clubes|title=SIC Notícias &#124; Federação Portuguesa de Futebol abre linha de crédito para apoiar clubes|website=SIC Notícias|date=16 March 2020 }}</ref>

On 28 April, [[Prime Minister of Portugal]] [[António Costa]] reunited with the presidents of the "[[Big Three (Portugal)|Big Three]]" clubs in Portugal ([[S.L. Benfica]], [[Sporting CP]] and [[FC Porto]]), the president of the FPF and the president of the LPFP to discuss the conditions of the return of football in Portugal.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.desporto.sapo.pt/amp/futebol/primeira-liga/artigos/antonio-costa-ja-esta-reunido-com-os-presidentes-da-fpf-liga-e-tres-grandes |title=António Costa já está reunido com os presidentes da FPF, Liga e 'três grandes' |access-date=23 May 2020 |archive-date=10 May 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200510104036/https://www.desporto.sapo.pt/amp/futebol/primeira-liga/artigos/antonio-costa-ja-esta-reunido-com-os-presidentes-da-fpf-liga-e-tres-grandes |url-status=dead }}</ref> The reunion caused some controversy for some Primeira Liga clubs such as [[S.C. Braga|Braga]] and [[Vitória S.C.|Vitória de Guimarães]], who were not satisfied that only the "Big Three" clubs were the only ones invited to the discussion, and instead believed all Primeira Liga clubs should have been invited.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ominho.pt/sc-braga-furioso-com-costa-por-so-ouvir-os-tres-grandes-de-guimaraes-tambem-chovem-criticas/|title=SC Braga furioso com Costa por só ouvir os 'três grandes'. De Guimarães também chovem críticas|date=28 April 2020|website=O Minho}}</ref> Two days later, António Costa approved the return of the league, with all matches being resumed [[Behind closed doors (sport)|behind closed doors]] following the consent of the Portuguese [[Ministry of Health (Portugal)|Ministry of Health]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.publico.pt/2020/04/30/desporto/noticia/siza-vieira-confirma-regresso-futebol-final-maio-1914636/amp|title=Governo autoriza I Liga e Taça de Portugal à porta fechada. II Liga cancelada|first=Marco|last=Vaza|date=30 April 2020|website=PÚBLICO}}</ref>

On 11 May, it was announced that several teams in the Primeira Liga had players tested positive for COVID-19, with Benfica having a player from its reserve team to be infected, followed by three players from [[F.C. Famalicão|Famalicão]], [[Moreirense F.C.|Moreirense]] and Vitória de Guimarães that were sent home and were isolated from the rest of their respective teams.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rtp.pt/noticias/desporto/covid-19-testes-detetam-varios-jogadores-positivos-na-i-liga_v1227755|title=Covid-19. Testes detetam vários jogadores positivos na I Liga|first=Rádio e Televisão de|last=Portugal|website=Covid-19. Testes detetam vários jogadores positivos na I Liga|date=11 May 2020 }}</ref> On 20 May, LPFP president Pedro Proença president proposed that following the restart of the league, the matches played should be shown on the [[free-to-air]] television station [[Radio e Televisão de Portugal|RTP]] in Portugal instead of the [[Pay television|pay TV]] subscriptions, with the backing of the [[Portuguese government]]. However, this proposal caused some controversy with the league's main sponsor, [[NOS (Portuguese company)|NOS]], and several other sponsors, as well as various other clubs in the league, most notably Benfica and Porto.<ref>{{cite web | last=Ventura | first=Mário Rui | title=Pedro Proença sugeriu jogos em sinal aberto e gerou mal-estar nos clubes e operadoras (Liga) | website=A Bola | date=2020-05-20 | url=https://www.abola.pt/nnh/2020-05-20/liga-pedro-proenca-sugeriu-jogos-em-sinal-aberto-e-gerou-mal-estar-nos-clubes-e-o/845466 | language=pt | access-date=2020-06-24}}</ref> This prompted rumours that Proença could be forced to end his term prematurely, rumours Proença later dismissed.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.record.pt/futebol/futebol-nacional/liga-nos/detalhe/pedro-proenca-nega-ma-relacao-com-vieira|title=Pedro Proença nega má relação com Vieira|website=www.record.pt}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | author=ZAP | title=Pedro Proença em risco na Liga de Clubes. Benfica e FC Porto pedem a saída imediata | website=ZAP | date=2020-05-21 | url=https://zap.aeiou.pt/pedro-proenca-risco-na-liga-clubes-325750 | language=pt | access-date=2020-06-24}}</ref> Later that month, Benfica left the board of LPFP due to the controversy.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.noticiasaominuto.com/desporto/1485149/benfica-deixa-direcao-da-liga-de-clubes|title=Benfica deixa direção da Liga de Clubes|date=22 May 2020|website=Notícias ao Minuto}}</ref>

On 14 May, after a meeting of all clubs, five substitutions will be permitted, which was temporarily allowed by [[International Football Association Board|IFAB]] following a proposal by [[FIFA]] to lessen the impact of fixture congestion.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/52443195 |title=Fifa proposes use of five substitutions to help with fixture congestion |date=27 April 2020 |access-date=7 May 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theifab.com/news/five-substitutes-option-temporarily-allowed-for-competition-organisers |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210514050706/https://theifab.com/news/five-substitutes-option-temporarily-allowed-for-competition-organisers |url-status=dead |archive-date=14 May 2021 |title=Five substitutes option temporarily allowed for competition organisers |work=[[International Football Association Board]] |date=8 May 2020 |access-date=9 May 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.dfb.de/news/detail/dfl-saison-notfalls-im-juli-zu-ende-spielen-215549/|title=DFL: Saison notfalls im Juli zu Ende spielen|work=dfb.de |date=14 May 2020 |access-date=14 May 2020}}</ref> On 22 May, the LPFP announced that the league would be resumed on 3 June.<ref name="auto"/> On 27 May, it was announced that one of the assistant referees for a league match between Benfica and [[C.S. Marítimo|Marítimo]] had tested positive for COVID-19, leading him to be replaced by another referee for the scheduled league match.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sicnoticias.pt/especiais/coronavirus/2020-05-27-Arbitro-Jose-Rodrigues-testou-positivo-a-Covid-19|title=Árbitro José Rodrigues testou positivo à Covid-19|date=27 May 2020 }}</ref>

On 30 May, the LPFP approved a plan to resume the league, but during the reunion between all clubs of the league, Marítimo refused to accept the five substitutions rules, leading the rule to be accepted on 8 June by the LPFP despite Marítimo's refusal.<ref>{{cite web | author=ZAP | title=Bronca na Liga. 5 substituições adiadas e Marítimo recusa assinar retoma | website=ZAP | date=2020-05-30 | url=https://zap.aeiou.pt/bronca-na-liga-contestacao-adia-5-substituicoes-maritimo-recusa-assinar-plano-retoma-327400 | language=pt | access-date=2020-06-24}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://eco.sapo.pt/2020/06/08/aprovadas-cinco-substituicoes-e-subidas-de-nacional-e-farense/|title=Aprovadas cinco substituições e subidas de Nacional e Farense &#124; ECO|website=eco.sapo.pt}}</ref>

==Teams==
Eighteen teams competed in the league – the top fifteen teams from [[2018–19 Primeira Liga|the previous season]], the two teams promoted from the [[2018–19 LigaPro|LigaPro]] ([[F.C. Paços de Ferreira|Paços de Ferreira]] and [[F.C. Famalicão|Famalicão]]) and one team promoted directly from the third-tier [[2018–19 Campeonato de Portugal|Campeonato de Portugal]] ([[Gil Vicente F.C.|Gil Vicente]]).
Paços de Ferreira came back to the top division one season after being relegated,<ref>{{cite web|date=20 April 2019|url=https://sol.sapo.pt/artigo/654166/pacos-de-ferreira-sobe-a-primeira-liga|title=Paços de Ferreira sobe à Primeira Liga|trans-title=Paços de Ferreira is promoted to Primeira Liga.|language=pt|website=Sol|access-date=29 April 2019}}</ref> while Famalicão secured their return after a 25-year absence.<ref>{{cite web|date=28 April 2019|url=https://www.rtp.pt/noticias/futebol-nacional/famalicao-sobe-a-i-liga-de-futebol-25-anos-depois_d1144163|title=Famalicão sobre à I Liga de Futebol 25 anos depois|trans-title=Famalicão is promoted to Primeira Liga 25 years after the last participation.|language=pt|website=[[Rádio e Televisão de Portugal|RTP]]|access-date=29 April 2019}}</ref> Gil Vicente, having been relegated to the third-level of Portuguese football in the 2018–19 season, were reinstated in the Primeira Liga by court decision, five years after their last participation.<ref>{{cite web|date=30 July 2018|url=https://www.jn.pt/desporto/interior/gil-vicente-na-i-liga-so-em-201920-9324504.html|title=Gil Vicente na Liga só em 2019/20|trans-title=Gil Vicente will only be in Primeira Liga by 2019/20|language=pt|website=[[Jornal de Notícias]]|access-date=30 July 2018}}</ref>
These three teams replaced [[G.D. Chaves|Chaves]], [[C.D. Feirense|Feirense]] (both relegated after three years in the top flight), and [[C.D. Nacional|Nacional]] (relegated one season after their promotion).
